judgment.rationale: Both are Class-2 Content statements (same canonical rank 1) under CG-1 but different competencies: 'Puzzles (numbers, shapes and measurements)' sits under C-1.13 (computational thinking through problem-solving strategies), while 'Classifies 2-D shapes based on their properties such as sides and corners' sits under C-1.3 (grouping objects by attributes/properties). Their coherence is substantive rather than merely lexical: the puzzle SFI's own Learning Component explicitly includes 'Solve shape puzzles using problem-solving strategies', which draws on and reinforces the attribute-based reasoning about shapes (sides, corners) expressed in the classification SFI. However, the puzzle statement is a broad, unspecified bullet covering numbers, shapes and measurements, and no source text establishes that shape classification is required for, or developmentally prior to, puzzle work at the same class rank; same-rank developmental direction is therefore not substantively supported in either direction. Symmetric conceptual/application coherence is the best-supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 34 omitted items) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so this reading rests on the bounded excerpts only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-1.3 (grouping objects by attributes). The Class-1 item (rank 0) asks children to classify objects by the simple observable attributes 'flat and round'; the Class-2 item (rank 1) requires classifying named concrete objects (chalk box, ball, ice cone, Rubik's cube) by flat and round/curved surfaces plus straight and round/curved edges and corners. The shared learning component 'Classify objects based on flat and round/curved surfaces' is common to both, while the Class-2 SFI adds two further components (edges, corners), showing substantive extension of the same classification skill to additional geometric features of 3-D objects. Proficiency in the Class-1 flat/round sorting supports success with the richer Class-2 surface/edge/corner classification, so lower-to-higher rank direction is supported. Evidence limitation: nomination evidence and both endpoints' source evidence are truncated, and merge/audit context applies to both endpoints and their ancestors, but the full statement texts and learning components supplied are sufficient for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same shape-attribute competency (C-3.1) and goal (CG-3), but they are substantively different tasks at different resolved ranks: Class-3 (rank 2) 'Draws / makes the 2-D shapes' (LCs: draw 2-D shapes, make 2-D shapes) and Class-4 (rank 3) 'Making 3-D shapes using nets (net of a cube, cuboid, cylinder)' (LCs: make a cube/cuboid/cylinder using its net). Constructing a solid from a net requires drawing and cutting out accurate 2-D plane figures and folding them, so proficiency in drawing/making 2-D shapes supports success in the later net-based 3-D construction; this is a substantive extension from plane figures to solids, not generic repetition. Direction follows the lower-to-higher class rank. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text and LCs.
